cover.title: The Tiny Fee That Eats Acorns

lines.text: A 1% fee can eat a quarter of your pile.
lines.say: A one percent fee can eat a quarter of your pile.

lines.text: Say squirrel plants $10,000, and it grows 7% a year before fees, for 30 years.
lines.say: Say squirrel plants ten thousand dollars, and it grows seven percent a year before fees, for thirty years.

lines.text: Almost every fund charges a yearly fee. It's called the expense ratio.
lines.say: Almost every fund charges a yearly fee. It's called the expense ratio.

lines.text: With no fee, squirrel ends with $76,123. With a 1% fee, $57,435.
lines.say: With no fee, squirrel ends with about seventy-six thousand. With a one percent fee, about fifty-seven thousand.

lines.text: Same tree. Same squirrel. $18,688 gone to fees: about a quarter.
lines.say: Same tree. Same squirrel. About eighteen thousand seven hundred dollars gone to fees. That's about a quarter.

lines.text: The fee comes out every year, so it compounds too. Squirrel is upset.
lines.say: The fee comes out every single year, so it compounds too. Squirrel is upset.

lines.text: Good news: average stock fund fees fell from 1.04% in 1996 to 0.40% in 2025.
lines.say: Good news: average stock fund fees fell from about one percent in nineteen ninety-six to zero point four percent in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: Index stock ETFs averaged just 0.14% in 2025.
lines.say: Index stock E T Fs averaged just zero point one four percent in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: Squirrel's rule: check the expense ratio before you plant.
lines.say: Squirrel's rule: check the expense ratio before you plant.

post.title: A 1% fund fee can eat a quarter of your pile in 30 years
post.ig:
A 1% fee can eat a quarter of your pile.
Say $10,000 grows 7% a year before fees for 30 years: $76,123 with no fee, $57,435 with a 1% fee. That's $18,688 gone, about 25%.
Average equity mutual fund fees fell from 1.04% in 1996 to 0.40% in 2025; index equity ETFs averaged 0.14% in 2025.
Sources: Investment Company Institute; SEC Investor.gov. The 7% return is an illustration, not a prediction.
News and education, not financial advice.
